status_summary: No HHS investigation of medical schools or the ACGME under Coats-Snowe, no opt-in communication to schools and no state-funding condition was found. HHS reorganized its Office for Civil Rights effective 2026-06-28, creating a Conscience and Religious Freedom Division whose listed statutes include the Coats-Snowe Amendment; that is an enforcement structure rather than any of the specific steps. A 2025-12-15 letter from members of Congress asked HHS and CMS to require opt-in abortion training as a condition of federal graduate medical education funding; no HHS response was found.

timeline.event: HHS Office for Civil Rights reorganization took effect (approved 2026-05-14, published 2026-06-30), creating a Conscience and Religious Freedom Division that enforces Coats-Snowe among other conscience laws.

title: Enforce Coats-Snowe in medical education and keep abortion training opt-in
uncertainties: The OCR reorganization notice was re-read in review: approved 2026-05-14, effective 2026-06-28, it replaces the Strategic Planning Division with a Conscience and Religious Freedom Division whose listed statutes include the Coats-Snowe Amendment (42 U.S.C. 238n); it does not mention medical schools, the ACGME or abortion training. The congressional letter of 2025-12-15 is a request, not an HHS action, and is not in the timeline. A March 2026 report of HHS investigating states over insurance coverage of abortion was seen in search results but concerns coverage laws, not medical education, and was not read. The FY 2027 Medicare inpatient payment rule contains a residency program nondiscrimination provision about race and other listed characteristics; no Coats-Snowe text was found in the portion read.
